text: あ、これは早くも見事な一品との出会いが
translation: Oh my — it seems I have encountered a truly splendid article already.

vocabulary.meaning: a single article; a fine piece

grammar: 〜が at the end of the sentence leaves the thought trailing off (sentence-final が), conveying wonder or exclamation rather than completing a clause.

text: これが噴水、命の源たる水をもてあそぶ / 罪深きアート
translation: So this is a fountain — a sinful work of art that toys with water, the very source of life.

vocabulary.meaning: to toy with; to play with frivolously

grammar: 罪深き is the classical (literary) attributive form of 罪深い, giving the speech an archaic, elevated register.

text: その魔性ゆえに効果を投げ入れたものの願いを
translation: And there are even some that will grant the wishes of those who toss a coin in, drawn by that bewitching power —

vocabulary.meaning: to toss in; to throw into

grammar: ゆえに is a formal/literary causal conjunction meaning 'because of' or 'on account of', elevating the register beyond the colloquial から or ので.

text: 叶えてしまうものまであるのか
translation: — to think there are actually such things.

vocabulary.meaning: to grant; to make (a wish) come true
thing; (here) such a thing (nominalizer with nuance of wonder)

grammar: 〜てしまう expresses completion with a nuance of surprise or astonishment ('to go so far as to…').

text: いいえ私この時のためにと意気込んで / 効果を少々持ってまいりました
translation: Oh no — I had psyched myself up for this very moment and brought along a modest number of coins.

vocabulary.meaning: to be enthusiastic; to psych oneself up
brought along (humble form of 持ってきました)

grammar: まいりました is the humble (謙譲語) past form of くる/いく, used here to humbly describe Elizabeth's own action of bringing coins.

text: 500円効果に数えまして2000枚 / 締めて100万円からスタートでございます
translation: Counting them at 500 yen per coin — 2,000 coins in all — for a grand total of one million yen to start with.

vocabulary.meaning: counting (polite conjunctive form of 数える)

grammar: 締めて is a set expression meaning 'all told' or 'totaling', used when summing up an amount.

text: あ / 肝心の願いを考えておりませんでした / これではいけませんね
translation: Oh — I had not thought of an actual wish to make. This simply will not do.

vocabulary.word: 考えておりませんでした
vocabulary.reading: かんがえておりませんでした
vocabulary.meaning: had not thought about (humble progressive past)
it won't do; that's no good

grammar: 〜ておりませんでした is the humble (謙譲語) negative past progressive of 〜ている, used by Elizabeth to humbly describe her own oversight.

text: 熟考の上また近いうちに訪れることにいたしましょう
translation: I shall give it careful thought and pay another visit before long.

vocabulary.meaning: before long; in the near future

grammar: 〜ことにいたしましょう is a humble volitional construction (いたす = humble する) expressing a decision or resolution: 'I shall (decide to)…'.

text: おや / こちらは何の施設でしょうか
translation: My, what sort of establishment might this be?

vocabulary.meaning: oh my; well (exclamation of mild surprise)
I wonder…; might it be…? (polite conjecture)

grammar: 〜でしょうか is a polite way of wondering aloud or asking a question, softer and more formal than ですか alone.

text: 中に険しいお顔立ちの御人がいらっしゃいますが
translation: Inside there appears to be a gentleman with a rather stern expression.

vocabulary.meaning: stern; fierce; harsh (of a face or expression)

grammar: いらっしゃいます is the honorific (尊敬語) form of いる, showing respect toward the person being described.

text: こちらに貼ってある顔写真は / 死ねいて敗、報奨金
translation: The photographs posted here show… 'Wanted — Dead or Alive — Reward Money'…

vocabulary.meaning: is posted; has been stuck up (resultant state)

grammar: 〜てある indicates a resultant state brought about by a deliberate prior action: 'posters have been put up (and remain so)'.

text: これは私の討伐依頼と同様のものと考えてよろしいのでしょうか
translation: I wonder — might this be something akin to the subjugation requests I receive?

vocabulary.word: よろしいのでしょうか
vocabulary.reading: よろしいのでしょうか
vocabulary.meaning: would it be all right to think so? (polite conjecture)

grammar: 〜と考えてよろしいのでしょうか is a formal/polite way of seeking confirmation: 'May I understand it as…?'

text: なるほど、池鳥でございますね / 特診いたしました
translation: I see — it is a police box, then. I have learned something new.

vocabulary.meaning: I see; indeed; so that's how it is
police box; koban (Elizabeth's reading is likely a mishearing of 交番)
special learning; here likely a mishearing/malapropism of 得心 (understanding/being convinced)

grammar: 〜いたしました is the humble past of する (いたす), used to describe Elizabeth's own act of understanding/learning.

text: こちらの建物はまさかここはクラブ / 内なるパトスのままに踊る
translation: This building — could it be… a club? A place where one dances in accordance with the passions within —

vocabulary.meaning: could it be; surely not (expression of surprise or conjecture)
pathos; passion (loanword from Greek via German)

grammar: 〜のままに is a formal construction meaning 'in accordance with' or 'as it is', here conveying 'dancing freely as one's inner passions dictate'.

text: そんな日常では許されぬ欲求を解放する光と音の地下庭
translation: — an underground garden of light and sound where one releases desires not permitted in ordinary daily life.

vocabulary.meaning: not permitted; not forgiven (literary negative of 許される)
to release; to liberate; to set free

grammar: 許されぬ is the classical literary negative attributive form of 許される (= 許されない), giving an elevated, poetic tone.

text: おっはっ 今はしまっているのです / 残念でございます ぜひ私
translation: Oh! It is closed right now — how disappointing. I was truly hoping to —
grammar: The sentence breaks off mid-thought (sentence-final truncation), conveying Elizabeth's eagerness that goes unstated — a rhetorical trailing-off.

text: 思っておりました
translation: …that is what I had been thinking.
grammar: 〜ておりました is the humble (謙譲語) past progressive of 〜ている, continuing the broken-off thought from the previous line.

text: 幾分気が収まりました それにしても
translation: I feel somewhat more settled now. Even so —

vocabulary.meaning: to calm down; to feel settled

grammar: それにしても is a conjunctive expression used to pivot or contrast: 'even granting all that, still…'

text: どの場所も大変興味深く目移りをしてしまいます よろしければあなたのおすすめを教えていただけません
translation: Every place here is so very fascinating that I find my attention pulled in all directions. If you don't mind, might you tell me your recommendations?

vocabulary.meaning: having one's attention caught by many things; being unable to choose

vocabulary.word: 教えていただけません
vocabulary.reading: おしえていただけません
vocabulary.meaning: could you not tell me? (humble request form)

grammar: 〜ていただけませんか is a humble request form: 'would you be so kind as to…?' Here the か is dropped, making it slightly softer.

text: カラオケ それはまさか私の秘密のレパート
translation: Karaoke — could that be… the perfect stage to unveil my secret reperto—

vocabulary.meaning: could it be; surely (conjecture or surprise)
repertoire (truncated loanword — レパートリー)

grammar: The word レパート is a clipped loanword (レパートリー), cut off mid-utterance for comic effect, indicating Elizabeth's excitement getting ahead of her speech.

text: お披露目の時が訪れたようですね 下部音曲の本職の歌い手にワンボタンで挑戦できるという
translation: It seems the time has come to make my debut. Apparently one can challenge professional singers of the lower musical arts with the press of a single button —

vocabulary.meaning: lower/folk musical arts; plebeian music (archaic/formal phrasing)

grammar: 〜という nominalizes and introduces a description or reported characteristic: 'the thing called…' or 'the fact that…'

text: あの / あ失礼 / 少々お待ちいただけますか こちらにも噴水があったのですね
translation: Um — oh, pardon me. Would you mind waiting just a moment? There was a fountain here as well, it seems.

vocabulary.word: お待ちいただけますか
vocabulary.reading: おまちいただけますか

vocabulary.meaning: so it seems; so that's how it is (seeking confirmation with a tone of discovery)

grammar: お待ちいただけますか combines the honorific prefix お〜, the verb 待つ, and the humble-honorific いただく to form a very polite request.

text: さらにあちらにも噴水が / なるほど この場所の噴水の主は三味一体ということなのですね
translation: And over there is yet another fountain — I see, so the master of the fountains in this place is a trinity in one.

vocabulary.meaning: trinity; three-in-one (a pun on 三位一体, the Holy Trinity)

grammar: 三味一体 is Elizabeth's playful (mis)use of 三位一体 (the Holy Trinity), substituting 味 (flavor/taste) for 位 (rank/position) — characteristic of her slightly off-kilter formal speech.

text: お待たせいたしました それでは参りましょう
translation: Thank you for waiting. Shall we be on our way?

vocabulary.word: お待たせいたしました
vocabulary.reading: おまたせいたしました
vocabulary.meaning: sorry to have kept you waiting (humble-honorific set phrase)
let us go (humble volitional of 行く)

grammar: お待たせいたしました is a fixed humble-honorific expression combining the honorific お〜 form and the humble いたす, conventionally used when rejoining someone after an absence.

text: では参りましょう 我が主をたたえる歌 / ぜひご一緒に
translation: Then let us proceed. A song in praise of my liege — please, do join in.

vocabulary.meaning: let us go (humble volitional of 行く/来る)
my lord; my master (archaic/formal first-person possessive)
to praise; to extol; to laud

grammar: 我が is a classical/literary first-person possessive pronoun (my/our), giving Elizabeth's speech an archaic, elevated formality befitting her character.

text: おや?ご存じない?
translation: Oh my? You're not familiar with it?

vocabulary.meaning: oh my; well (expression of mild surprise)

grammar: ご存じ is the honorific form of 知っている; the question form ない? is a gentle inquiry implying surprise that the other person doesn't know.

text: 本日は数々の貴重な体験をさせていただきました / 依頼の方は12分に達成でございます
translation: Today I was afforded a great many precious experiences, and I am pleased to report that your request has been fulfilled to the fullest.

vocabulary.meaning: more than sufficiently; to the fullest

grammar: させていただきました is a humble expression (〜させていただく) used to humbly describe an action done with another's permission or grace; でございます is a formal copula.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If it would please you, I would very much like the honor of accompanying you again sometime.

vocabulary.meaning: if it is agreeable to you; if you don't mind
I think/feel (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます is a highly formal, layered expression of desire: 〜させていただく (humble request to be allowed to do something) + たく (desiderative) + 存じます (humble verb for thinking/feeling).

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been awaiting you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました is a humble continuous past construction: お待ちする (humble 待つ) + おりました (humble past of いる), conveying polite anticipation.

text: 行く手に歯向かい流れてくる階段
translation: Stairs that flow against you, approaching as you advance.
grammar: This is a poetic, noun-phrase-style description (no main verb). 歯向かい modifies the overall image of the escalator steps moving against the direction of travel.

text: これがエスカレーター / シンプルでありながら見た目以上の消耗を強いられる試練
translation: So this is an escalator — simple in appearance, yet an ordeal that demands far greater exertion than one would expect.
grammar: 〜ながら here is concessive ('although; despite being'), contrasting the simple appearance with the demanding reality: シンプルでありながら = 'while being simple.'

text: おや?良い子の皆様が危険とのことです / 我々も注意して参りましょう
translation: Oh my? It seems this is considered dangerous for well-behaved children — let us also take care as we proceed.

vocabulary.meaning: let us go; let us proceed (humble volitional)

grammar: 〜とのことです conveys information heard or reported from a source ('I understand that…; it is said that…'), here referring to a warning sign.

text: そしてこれは? / 足元にお気を付けください / この先に落とし穴がございます
translation: And what is this? 'Please watch your step' — there is a pitfall ahead.

vocabulary.meaning: one's feet; footing; the ground underfoot

grammar: Elizabeth reads a warning sign aloud as a continuous utterance; the three fragments form one logical statement — noticing the sign, reading it, and announcing its meaning.

text: こちらでございます 柵で囲まれたこの中心にでございます
translation: It is right here — in the very center, enclosed by a fence.
grammar: こちらでございます is a polite way to point something out ('it is here/this way'); the second clause further specifies the location with 柵で囲まれたこの中心に ('in the center enclosed by a fence').

text: 目を引く看板で囲んだ上立ち入り禁止の文字ですが人は往々に禁じられたものほど触れてみたくなる
translation: Surrounded by eye-catching signage, the words 'No Entry' are displayed — yet people tend to feel all the more compelled to touch that which is forbidden.

vocabulary.meaning: often; generally; as is often the case

grammar: 〜ほど〜なる is a proportional pattern: 'the more X, the more Y' — here, 禁じられたものほど触れてみたくなる, 'the more something is forbidden, the more one wants to touch it.'

text: 落とし穴は隠すものという常識を逆手に取った高度なトラップでございます
translation: It is a sophisticated trap that turns on its head the common wisdom that pitfalls are meant to be hidden.

vocabulary.meaning: to turn against; to use something to one's advantage; to exploit

grammar: 〜という常識を逆手に取る means 'to exploit/subvert the conventional wisdom that ~'; でございます closes the sentence with Elizabeth's characteristic formal register.

text: 流れる足場に加えて心理トラップを組み合わせた落とし穴
translation: A pitfall that combines a moving foothold with a psychological trap.
grammar: This is a nominal sentence (no copula at the end), delivered as an analytical summary — Elizabeth synthesizing her observations about the escalator-as-trap into a single descriptive phrase.

text: 街の治安を守るとはかくも大変なことなのでございますね
translation: Maintaining public order in a city is truly an enormously demanding undertaking, is it not.

vocabulary.meaning: so; this much; to such a degree (literary)

grammar: かくも is a slightly literary/archaic intensifier meaning 'so much; to this extent,' fitting Elizabeth's formal speech style; のでございますね adds reflective, wondering nuance.

text: 胸を打たれております / この街を愛する見知らぬどなたかの思いを噛みしめつつ
translation: I am deeply moved — savoring the feelings of some unknown person who loves this city.

vocabulary.meaning: to be deeply moved; to be touched
to savor; to take to heart; to chew over deeply

grammar: 〜つつ is a literary connective meaning 'while doing ~'; here 噛みしめつつ = 'while savoring/reflecting deeply on,' adding a sense of lingering emotional contemplation.

text: それでは参りましょう
translation: Well then, shall we be on our way.

vocabulary.meaning: let us go (humble volitional of 行く/来る)

grammar: 参る is the humble form of 行く/来る; the volitional 〜ましょう makes it an invitation ('let us go'), with それでは ('well then') as a polite transition marker.

text: これはこのかぐわしい香りはまさか
translation: This — this fragrant aroma — could it possibly be…?

vocabulary.meaning: surely not; could it possibly be…

grammar: The sentence trails off with まさか, creating dramatic suspense; the repetition of これは…このかぐわしい香りは is a self-interrupting, escalating realization — Elizabeth's wonder building mid-sentence.

text: はあ驚いたわ / この具の秘密匂いだけでわかるんか / 姉ちゃん、だってにおもろい格好しとらんな
translation: Whoa, amazing! You can tell what's in it just from the smell? Hey, miss — you're dressed pretty weird, aren't ya.

vocabulary.meaning: interesting; funny (Kansai dialect for おもしろい)

grammar: The vendor speaks in Kansai dialect: おもろい (= おもしろい), しとらんな (= していないね). This contrasts with Elizabeth's formal standard Japanese, highlighting her otherworldliness.

text: ま、たこ焼き屋はたこ以外焼いたらあかんなんて法律あらへん / で、ちんとこう立ってや / ほっぺた落っこちてまうね
translation: Well, there's no law saying a takoyaki stall can't grill things other than octopus — so stand right there, nice and straight! It'll knock your socks off.

vocabulary.meaning: not okay; must not (Kansai dialect for いけない/ダメ)
there isn't (Kansai dialect for ない)

vocabulary.word: ほっぺた落っこちてまう
vocabulary.reading: ほっぺたおっこちてまう
vocabulary.meaning: your cheeks will fall off (expression: it's so delicious you'll be overwhelmed)

grammar: ほっぺたが落ちる is a colloquial expression meaning food is so delicious it makes your cheeks 'drop' (overwhelmingly tasty); 〜てまう is a Kansai form of 〜てしまう (completion/regret nuance).

text: ほっぺたが落ちる料理 / 現実には非常事態のような気もいたしますね / ぜひとも体験してみたく存じます
translation: A dish that makes one's cheeks fall off — in reality, that sounds rather like an emergency situation. I do so wish to experience it for myself.

vocabulary.meaning: by all means; absolutely; without fail

grammar: Elizabeth takes the idiom ほっぺたが落ちる literally, treating it as a medical event — her naive literalism played for comedic effect. 〜てみたく存じます is a humble, formal way to express a wish to try something.

text: ですがあいにく持ち合わせはこちらだけ
translation: However, I'm afraid this is all I happen to have on me.

vocabulary.meaning: unfortunately; regrettably; as bad luck would have it
what one happens to have on hand; ready cash

grammar: 持ち合わせ refers to money or items one currently has on their person; こちらだけ ('only this') implies she is presenting an unusual or insufficient form of payment.

text: これでどうにかお売りいただけるでしょうか
translation: Would you be willing to sell me some with this?

vocabulary.meaning: somehow; by some means; if at all possible

vocabulary.word: お売りいただけるでしょうか
vocabulary.reading: おうりいただけるでしょうか
vocabulary.meaning: would you be so kind as to sell (to me) — very polite request

grammar: お〜いただけるでしょうか is a highly formal, layered request: honorific prefix お + いただく (humble 'to receive') + potential + でしょうか (polite conjecture), softening the ask to its most deferential form.

text: 私実際にほっぺたを落としている方をお見かけしたことがございません / おそらく市政のものには安々と手出しできない価格
translation: I have never actually witnessed anyone whose cheeks have fallen off — it is likely priced beyond the easy reach of ordinary citizens.

vocabulary.meaning: to happen to see; to catch sight of (humble/polite)
municipal administration; city government (here used loosely for 'ordinary citizens/public')
to get involved with; to lay hands on; to purchase

grammar: Elizabeth reasons (humorously and naively) that because no one's cheeks have literally fallen off in her presence, the takoyaki must be prohibitively expensive. おそらく introduces her polite conjecture.

text: は?よく見ましたらワンパック400円 / はっ
translation: Wha—? Upon closer inspection, one pack is 400 yen — ah!

vocabulary.meaning: upon looking closely; when I looked carefully
ah! (gasp of sudden realization or surprise)

grammar: 〜ましたら is a polite conditional/temporal ('when/upon doing'); here よく見ましたら = 'when I looked closely.' The trailing はっ signals Elizabeth's sudden realization — she can afford it after all.

text: そ、それでは、2パックほどお願いいたします
translation: Th-then… I would like two packs, if you please.
grammar: お願いいたします is the most formal/humble standard request phrase: お願い (honorific noun from 願う) + いたす (humble form of する) + ます. The stuttered そ、それでは suggests flustered excitement.

text: はい、ギニー、また来てや
translation: There ya go! Come again!

vocabulary.meaning: here you go (Kansai dialect variant of はい, どうぞ)
come again! (Kansai dialect: や is a softening particle)

grammar: また来てや is Kansai dialect for また来てね ('come again'); the vendor's casual Kansai speech contrasts sharply with Elizabeth's formal Tokyo-standard Japanese throughout the scene.

text: このプリプリした凶器に覆われた独特の食感は間違いなくあれ?
translation: This unique texture, covered in that plump, jiggly coating — this must certainly be that, isn't it?
grammar: 〜に覆われた modifies 食感 as a relative clause; 間違いなく＋あれ with rising intonation forms a rhetorical confirmation question ('that must be...!').

text: よもや食材として出会う時が来るとは驚きでございます
translation: I am truly surprised that the day would come when I encounter it as an ingredient.
grammar: よもや〜とは is a set expression of surprised disbelief: 'to think that [X] would happen...' The conditional とは marks an unexpected realization.

text: いいえ特には何も / ですが私食べてみたいものは他にもまだまだございます
translation: No, nothing in particular — but there are still many more things I would like to try eating.

vocabulary.meaning: still a long way to go, many more
there are (polite form of ある)

grammar: Two fragments joined by / form one turn: a brief denial (いいえ特には何も) followed by an elaborating concessive with ですが ('but...').

text: 考えてみればそれらを食事を得るまで / ほっぺたを失うわけにはまいりません
translation: Come to think of it, I cannot afford to lose my cheeks before I have eaten all of those things.

vocabulary.meaning: come to think of it, if I think about it
cannot do (humble-polite negative of いく/くる)

grammar: 〜わけにはまいりません is a polite emphatic construction meaning 'I simply cannot do [X]'; it expresses strong obligation or constraint.

text: この近辺にはまだまだ飲食の場がある様子 / はしごというのをしてもよろしいでしょうか
translation: It seems there are still many more dining establishments nearby — would it be all right if we went bar-hopping?

vocabulary.meaning: dining establishment, place to eat and drink
bar-hopping, going from place to place (lit. ladder)
would it be all right? (polite request for permission)

grammar: 〜様子 ('it appears that...') expresses inference from observation; はしごというのをしてもよろしいでしょうか is a polite permission request wrapping a noun-phrase with という.

text: まずは漫画喫茶と呼ばれる場所にある ドリンクバーなる食材から参りましょう
translation: Let us begin with the ingredient known as a drink bar, found at a place called a manga café.

vocabulary.meaning: manga café (café stocked with manga to read)
ingredient (Elizabeth charmingly treats drinks as foodstuffs)
let us go; let us begin (humble volitional)

grammar: 〜と呼ばれる is a relative clause ('called/known as'); 〜から参りましょう means 'let us start from/with [X]'.

text: 混合比によって無限の味が生み出せるというドリンクバー
translation: A drink bar, from which infinite flavors can be created depending on the mixing ratio.

vocabulary.meaning: can produce, can bring forth (potential form)

grammar: 〜によって marks the causal agent ('depending on / by means of'); the sentence is a noun-phrase appositive — the subject ドリンクバー is restated in elaboration.

text: 想像しただけで心持ちが高ぶるのを感じます
translation: Just imagining it, I feel my heart beginning to race with excitement.

vocabulary.meaning: to be excited, to be stirred up

grammar: 〜のを感じます ('I feel [X] happening') takes a nominalized clause as its object; 〜だけで ('just by doing') expresses sufficiency of the condition.

text: なるほど
translation: I see.

vocabulary.meaning: I see, indeed, that makes sense

text: なんとまぁ
translation: My, my.

vocabulary.meaning: my goodness, well I never, how surprising

text: これはまった
translation: Oh, this is—

vocabulary.meaning: Oh, this is... (truncated exclamation of surprise; likely これはまった, a cut-off utterance)

text: これでこのあたりの料理はすべて食べ尽くしたようでございます
translation: It seems I have now eaten every dish in this area.
grammar: 〜尽くす as a compound verb suffix means 'to do [X] completely/to exhaustion'; ようでございます is the polite form of ようだ expressing inference.

text: あのどうかなさいましたか / 思えば7食目あたりからあまりお箸が進んでおられないご様子でしたが
translation: Oh, is something the matter? Come to think of it, it seemed as though your chopsticks had not been moving much from around the seventh meal onward.

vocabulary.word: どうかなさいましたか
vocabulary.reading: どうかなさいましたか
vocabulary.meaning: is something the matter? (honorific, polite inquiry)

grammar: お箸が進んでおられない is a double-polite construction: the honorific おられる (= いる) combined with negation, observing the protagonist's eating; 〜あたりから indicates a starting point ('from around the Nth time').

text: ともあれ本日は文字通りのおいしい体験をありがとうございました
translation: In any case, thank you very much for a truly delicious experience today — in the most literal sense of the word.

vocabulary.meaning: in any case, be that as it may

grammar: 〜をありがとうございました is a formal expression of thanks for a specific thing; 文字通りの modifies 体験, allowing Elizabeth to note she is using the word 'delicious' literally.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If you would like, I do hope we might have the pleasure of going out together again someday.

vocabulary.meaning: if it is agreeable to you, if you would like

vocabulary.word: ご一緒させていただく
vocabulary.reading: ごいっしょさせていただく
vocabulary.meaning: to accompany (humble request to be allowed to join)
I think/feel (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます is an extremely polite volitional: 'I humbly wish to be permitted to do [X]'; it combines the causative-passive いただく with the humble 存じます.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been waiting for you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました is the humble continuous past: お待ちする (humble 待つ) + おる (humble いる) in past tense, expressing respectful anticipation.

text: ここが寺院によく似た施設 神社ですね / 確かにシャドウなどとはまた違った / 神秘的で新たかな気配がいたします
translation: So this is a shrine — a facility very similar to a temple. Indeed, it gives off a mystical, fresh atmosphere quite different from that of Shadows.
grammar: 〜とはまた違った ('different again from [X]') uses とは for contrast; 新たかな is an archaic/literary adjectival form of 新たな ('fresh, new'), befitting Elizabeth's formal register.

text: ではこちらの様式にのったりましてまずは参拝をいたしましょう
translation: Now then, let us follow the customs of this place and begin with a visit to the shrine.

vocabulary.meaning: to follow, to conform to (a rule or custom)

grammar: 〜にのっとりまして is the te-form of のっとる ('to follow/conform to') in polite register; it functions as a conjunctive ('following the customs, we shall...').

text: このくらいでしょうか
translation: Is about this much right?

vocabulary.meaning: about this much, approximately this amount

text: ひとまず納め終えました / これで日頃はこちらの住人でない私にも / ご利益が訪れますでしょうか
translation: For the time being, I have finished making my offering — I wonder whether blessings will come even to me, who does not ordinarily reside here.

vocabulary.meaning: for the time being, for now
to finish offering/depositing (e.g. a coin at a shrine)

grammar: 〜でない私にも ('even to me who is not [X]') uses the negative relative clause でない modifying 私; 訪れますでしょうか is a formal speculative question ('I wonder if [blessings] will come').

text: 考えてみるとこの再生という仕組みは
translation: Come to think of it, this mechanism of regeneration—

vocabulary.meaning: come to think of it, when I think about it

grammar: The sentence trails off (sentence-final noun + は with no predicate), indicating Elizabeth is mid-thought, about to elaborate in the next line.

text: 噴水のそれとよく似ておりますね / そこかしこに人々の幸福をかなえるスポットがある / 素敵な土地にお住まいなのですね
translation: It closely resembles that of a fountain, doesn't it. There are spots for fulfilling people's happiness here and there — you really do live in a wonderful place.
grammar: The first clause (〜それとよく似ておりますね) continues the thought left trailing in idx 70; そこかしこに ('here and there') is an idiomatic adverbial phrase.

text: あちらにたくさん結ばれている紙の帯は / もしかし
translation: Those paper strips tied over there in such numbers — could they possibly be—

vocabulary.meaning: could it be (truncated もしかして — cut off mid-sentence)

grammar: The sentence is intentionally cut off (もしかし — truncated もしかして), creating suspense answered in the next line; this is a dramatic pause in dialogue.

text: やはり私の期待通りおみくじでございます
translation: Just as I expected — they are indeed omikuji fortune slips.

vocabulary.meaning: fortune slip drawn at a shrine or temple

grammar: やはり〜でございます expresses that reality matched expectation ('just as I thought'); 私の期待通り places the possessive to emphasize Elizabeth's personal anticipation.

text: 自らの運命をあえて紙切れ一枚に託し / そのリスク感を楽しむ遊戯と伺いましたが
translation: I have heard it is a game in which one dares to entrust one's fate to a single slip of paper and enjoys the thrill of that risk.

vocabulary.meaning: daringly, purposely, going out of one's way to
scrap of paper, slip of paper
to entrust, to leave something in someone's care

grammar: 〜と伺いましたが is the humble form of 聞く ('I have heard that...'), with が leaving the sentence open-ended (inviting confirmation or comment); あえて〜に託し is a conjunctive phrase meaning 'daring to entrust [fate] to...'.

text: なるほど運命について様々に書いてあるようですね
translation: I see — it seems there is quite a variety written here about fate.
grammar: 〜てあるようですね: 〜てある indicates a state resulting from a deliberate action; ようですね softens it to an inference/observation ('it seems that...').

text: では一つ私も引いてみたいと存じます / 全種類コンプリートするまで少々お待ちください
translation: Well then, I should like to draw one myself — please wait just a moment while I complete the full collection.

vocabulary.meaning: I think/wish (humble form of 思う)

grammar: 〜たいと存じます: ultra-polite volitional expression ('I humbly wish to do ~'), combining 〜たい (desire) with the humble verb 存じます.

text: あの先ほどから気になっておりましたが
translation: Um, I have been rather curious about something for a little while now.

vocabulary.meaning: a little while ago, just now
to be curious about, to weigh on one's mind

grammar: 〜から気になっておりました: 〜ておりました is the polite/humble progressive past of 〜ている, expressing a state that has been ongoing ('I have been curious since...').

text: あちらにあるものは何なのでしょうか
translation: What might that thing over there be?
grammar: 〜のでしょうか: a polite, wondering question form ('I wonder what it might be'), softer than 〜ですか.

text: これは確かこちらが滑り台で / こちらがジャングルジム 誠の神前には形ばかりのおごそかさなど不要
translation: If I recall correctly, this one is the slide and that one is the jungle gym — before the truest of altars, mere surface solemnity is wholly unnecessary.

vocabulary.meaning: before the gods, in front of a shrine

grammar: 形ばかりの〜など不要: 形ばかり means 'merely superficial/for form's sake'; など dismisses it as unworthy; together they assert that hollow formality has no place here.

text: なんと寛大で本質に満ちた姿勢でしょう
translation: What a magnanimous and thoroughly principled attitude that is.
grammar: なんと〜でしょう: an exclamatory structure ('how ~ it is!'), expressing admiration or surprise.

text: でしたら早速
translation: In that case, let us proceed right away.

vocabulary.meaning: in that case, if so (polite conditional)

text: これは楽しみを得るにはまず同じだけ登らねばならない / 世の節理を無言にして教える奥深い遊具でございます
translation: To obtain joy one must first climb an equal distance — this is a profound piece of play equipment that teaches the principles of the world without a single word.

vocabulary.meaning: principles, the natural order of things

grammar: 〜ねばならない: a formal/literary version of 〜なければならない, meaning 'must do ~', expressing obligation or necessity.

text: なかなかでございました / ではこちらのジャングルジムについても教えていただけますか
translation: That was quite something indeed. Now, might you tell me about this jungle gym as well?

vocabulary.word: 教えていただけますか
vocabulary.reading: おしえていただけますか
vocabulary.meaning: could you please tell/teach me (humble request)

grammar: 〜ていただけますか: a humble request form ('could you please do ~ for me?'), more deferential than 〜てくれますか.

text: 出られません
translation: I cannot get out.

vocabulary.meaning: cannot get out, am unable to exit

grammar: 〜られません: potential negative ('cannot do ~'); 出る → 出られる (can exit) → 出られません (cannot exit).

text: これはバランスが難しい
translation: Keeping one's balance on this is quite difficult.

text: 本日は今までの外出にもまして楽しみました
translation: I enjoyed today's outing more than any of our outings thus far.

vocabulary.meaning: I enjoyed (past tense of 楽しむ)

grammar: 〜にもまして: a comparative phrase meaning 'even more than ~', used to indicate surpassing a prior standard ('more than ever before').

text: 私実は近頃思うのですが / 私がこちらの世界を楽しく感じるのは
translation: I have been thinking lately — is the reason I find this world so enjoyable

vocabulary.meaning: to feel enjoyable, to find something fun

grammar: 〜のですが: the の nominalizes the preceding clause; ですが leaves the sentence incomplete/trailing, signaling that a continuation follows.

text: ただ新鮮な刺激があるからなのでしょうか
translation: simply because there are fresh and novel stimuli to be had?
grammar: 〜からなのでしょうか: a wondering question structure ('could it be because ~?'), combining the causal から, nominalizing の, and the speculative でしょうか.

text: もしかすると私 / あなたにお供する時間が楽しい
translation: Or perhaps... it is the time I spend accompanying you that I find so enjoyable —
grammar: もしかすると〜かもしれません (split across 89–90): a tentative conjecture structure ('it may perhaps be that ~'), expressing a soft, uncertain possibility.

text: ということなのかもしれません
translation: — that may very well be the case.
grammar: 〜ということなのかもしれません: ということ nominalizes the prior statement into a proposition; なのかもしれません adds polite conjecture ('it may indeed be that...').

text: ともあれまずは私どもの部屋に鉄棒など置いていただけないかと / 主に掛け合う所存でございます
translation: At any rate, I intend to first petition the Master to have a horizontal bar or the like installed in our room.

vocabulary.meaning: at any rate, be that as it may

grammar: 〜所存でございます: a very formal expression of intent or resolution ('it is my intention to ~'), used in written and highly polished speech.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If you would be so kind, I should very much like to go out together with you again someday.

vocabulary.meaning: if it pleases you, if you don't mind

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます: a chain of humility markers — させていただく (humbly doing something with permission) + たく (desire form) + 存じます (humble verb) — producing an extremely deferential request.

text: ではそろそろお開きといたしましょう
translation: Well then, I suppose it is about time we brought things to a close.
grammar: 〜といたしましょう: polite volitional form of 〜とする ('let us do ~'), using the humble いたす in place of する.

text: ですがその前に滑り台をワンモアお願いしたく
translation: However, before we do, I should like to request one more go on the slide.
grammar: 〜たく (verb stem + たく): a literary/formal truncated desire form of 〜たい ('I wish to ~'), leaving the sentence trailing in a soft, polite request.

text: せっかくですので2人乗りなどいかがですか
translation: Since we have the opportunity, how about we ride it together — the two of us?

vocabulary.meaning: since we're here / taking the opportunity

grammar: せっかくですので: 'since we have this rare opportunity' — せっかく carries a nuance of making the most of a situation that has been set up.

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been waiting for you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました

grammar: お〜しておりました: humble honorific verb construction (お + verb stem + する) in the progressive past, expressing respectful waiting on behalf of the speaker.

text: ここがあなたの学び屋 / 月光館学園ですね / この明るく美しい場所がカルタロスに返じるとは
translation: So this is your school — Gekkoukan High School. To think that this bright and beautiful place transforms into Tartarus…

vocabulary.reading: げっこうかんがくえん

vocabulary.meaning: to revert to, to transform back into

grammar: 〜とは: a topic-marking particle expressing surprise or strong impression ('to think that ~' / 'the fact that ~ is astonishing').

text: 私驚きを隠せません
translation: I cannot conceal my astonishment.
grammar: 〜を隠せません: 'cannot hide ~'; the potential negative 隠せない (from 隠す) expresses an involuntary inability to suppress a feeling.

text: これは困りました / 皆様ご提携の服をお召しの様子
translation: Oh dear, this is a problem — it appears that everyone is wearing the school uniform.

vocabulary.meaning: this is troubling, I am in a fix

grammar: お召しの様子: お召し is the honorific form of 着る (to wear); 様子 adds 'it appears/seems', making the observation polite and slightly indirect.

text: 私はいささか目立つようでございますね / 何事もなければ良いのですね
translation: It seems I stand out rather conspicuously — it would be best if nothing comes of it, I suppose.

vocabulary.meaning: to stand out, to attract attention

grammar: 〜ようでございます: polite conjecture (「〜ようだ」+ ございます); 〜ければ良い: conditional "it would be good if not."

text: では目立たないよう工夫を凝らすことにいたしましょう
translation: Very well, let me endeavor to make myself less conspicuous.

vocabulary.meaning: to devise a scheme, to put careful thought into
let us do (humble volitional of する)

grammar: 〜ことにいたしましょう: polite volitional expressing a decision to do something (humble form of 〜ことにしましょう).

text: こうして背中に隠れていればおおむね安心でございますね
translation: If I hide myself behind your back like this, I should be more or less safe, I believe.
grammar: 〜ていれば: conditional gerund expressing "if (one) is doing/staying in this state."

text: では校舎の中に向かいましょう
translation: Now then, let us make our way inside the school building.

vocabulary.meaning: let us head toward (volitional of 向かう)

grammar: 〜に向かいましょう: polite volitional indicating direction of movement.

text: これは驚きです。学校にもこのような販売施設に。
translation: How surprising — even within a school, there is a retail establishment such as this.
grammar: 〜にも: "even in/at ~" — the particle も adds the nuance of unexpectedness.

text: 少々お待ちいただけますか。私、前々から気になっておりましたものは。
translation: Could you wait just a moment? There is something I have been curious about for quite some time.

vocabulary.meaning: for a long time, for quite a while
to be curious about, to be on one's mind

grammar: 〜ていただけますか: humble request form ("could you please ~" — more polite than 〜てもらえますか).

text: 失礼いたします。給食を売っていただきたいのですが。
translation: Excuse me. I should like to purchase some school lunch, if you would be so kind.

vocabulary.meaning: excuse me (formal, humble apology for intruding)
I would like you to sell (to me) — humble request

grammar: 〜ていただきたいのですが: polite, softened request — the のですが trails off, implying a wish without being overly direct.

text: うーん、はい?
translation: Hmm... pardon?

text: 学校で飲み口にすることができると言われる給食を味わってみたかったのですが
translation: I had wished to taste the school lunch that is said to be something one can enjoy here at school.

vocabulary.meaning: taste, flavor (lit. "drinking mouth"); here likely used loosely for flavor/experience)
to taste, to savor, to experience

grammar: 〜てみたかったのですが: past-tense desire form (〜てみたい + past + のですが), politely expressing a wish; のですが softens and contextualizes.

text: パンも昼食時の醍醐味と聞き及びました
translation: I have also heard that the bread is one of the great pleasures of lunchtime.

vocabulary.meaning: the real thrill/pleasure of something, the best part
to have heard of, to come to know by hearsay (formal)

grammar: 〜と聞き及びました: formal way of saying "I have heard that ~" (聞き及ぶ is more literary than 聞く).

text: パンにいたしましょう
translation: I shall have the bread, then.

vocabulary.meaning: I shall do; let us do (humble volitional)

grammar: 〜にいたしましょう: humble volitional expressing a choice/decision ("I shall go with ~").

text: 念願かなったところで次へと参りましょう
translation: Now that my long-cherished wish has been fulfilled, let us move on to the next.

vocabulary.meaning: to be realized, to come true (of a wish)
let us go (humble volitional of 行く)

grammar: 念願かなったところで〜: "now that the wish has come true" — ところで here means "at the point where / now that."

text: これからの順路ですがまずはあなたの教室を覗いてみたく存じます
translation: As for our route from here, I should first like to take a peek inside your classroom.

vocabulary.meaning: to peek into, to look in
I humbly think/feel (humble form of 思う/知る)

grammar: 〜てみたく存じます: humble desire form — 〜たく (literary desiderative stem) + 存じます (humble copula), more formal than 〜てみたいと思います.

text: ここが教室 / わずかこれだけの広さの中に机の数だけの人数が強制するとは
translation: So this is the classroom — to think that a number of people equal to the desks are compelled to gather in a space as small as this.
grammar: 〜とは: exclamatory topic particle expressing surprise or wonder; 「机の数だけの人数」= "a number of people equal to the number of desks" (だけ = exactly that many).

text: いえ違いますね / 他者と調和する力を育むため / わざとこのように奥深い配慮を感じます
translation: No, that cannot be right — I sense a profound and intentional consideration here: to cultivate in each person the capacity to harmonize with others.

vocabulary.meaning: to harmonize, to be in accord
to nurture, to cultivate, to foster

grammar: わざと〜: "intentionally, on purpose" — here Elizabeth reinterprets the cramped classroom as a deliberate pedagogical design; 〜を感じます: "I feel/sense ~."

text: この監視用の物見台が俗に申します
translation: This observation platform used for supervision — it is what they commonly call...

vocabulary.meaning: as it is commonly called (俗に = colloquially; 申す = humble verb for 言う)

grammar: 俗に申します: formal/humble phrasing for "as people commonly say" or "what is commonly called" — the sentence trails off, anticipating a noun.

text: 教団でございますね / 確かに
translation: ...the teacher's podium, I believe. Yes, indeed.

vocabulary.meaning: teacher's podium, lectern at the front of a classroom

grammar: でございますね: polite copula (〜です) in its most formal register, with ね seeking gentle confirmation.

text: ここに立つと思わず教鞭を取りたい誘惑に駆られます
translation: Standing here, I find myself irresistibly tempted to take up the teacher's pointer.

vocabulary.meaning: to teach, to take up the pointer (lit. "to take up the teaching whip"; set phrase for teaching)
to be driven by, to be seized by (a feeling)

grammar: 思わず〜に駆られます: "involuntarily/unthinkably, I am seized by ~" — 思わず means "without thinking, reflexively."

text: 第1問
translation: Question one.

vocabulary.meaning: question number one, the first question

text: ダイエットフードとダイエットフード貝
translation: Diet food, and Diet Food Kai.

vocabulary.meaning: shellfish, clam; here likely a product name suffix ("Kai" version)

text: 美味しいのはどちらでしょう
translation: Which of the two is more delicious?

vocabulary.meaning: which (of two) — polite form of どっち

grammar: 〜でしょう: polite conjecture/question — here used rhetorically as a quiz question.

text: 正解でございます / 見事正解を選ばれたあなたには景品のダイエットフード貝を申請いたします
translation: That is correct! To you, who have splendidly chosen the right answer, I shall bestow the prize: Diet Food Kai.

vocabulary.meaning: I shall present/submit — here used whimsically for "I shall award"

grammar: 正解を選ばれたあなたには: honorific passive (〜られた) used to elevate the listener's action — "you, who have chosen the correct answer."

text: 授業とはおおむねこのような形でよろしいのでしょうか
translation: Is this more or less the form that a class generally takes?

vocabulary.meaning: acceptable, all right (polite form of いい)

grammar: 〜のでしょうか: polite rhetorical or genuine question seeking confirmation — softer than 〜ですか.

text: そろそろ後期の目線が気になってまいりましたので他へ移動しましょう
translation: I have begun to feel the gaze of those around us, so let us move along somewhere else.

vocabulary.meaning: to start to bother one, to become conscious of

grammar: 〜てまいりました: humble progressive + past, indicating a gradual change of state — "I have come to feel ~" (まいる as humble form of くる).

text: 人間型の石膏像が中身が出てこないよう石膏で固めているのでしょうか / 少々窮屈に思いますが
translation: I wonder — are human-shaped plaster statues sealed in plaster to keep what is inside from coming out? That seems rather confining, I must say.

vocabulary.meaning: to harden, to solidify, to seal

grammar: 〜よう（に）固めている: "sealed/hardened so that ~" — ように here indicates purpose or prevention (〜ないよう = "so as not to"); Elizabeth naively wonders if the figure inside is being contained.

text: ピアノでしたら多少は覚えがございます
translation: When it comes to piano, I do have some recollection of it.

vocabulary.meaning: polite form of ある (to exist/have)

grammar: 〜でしたら is a conditional/topic-setting form ('when it comes to / if it's about'), more polished than 〜なら.

text: ベルベットの歌 / ご存知ですね
translation: You are familiar with the Velvet song, aren't you?
grammar: ご存知ですね uses the honorific prefix ご with 存知 (知っている in humble/honorific form), asking for confirmation with ね.

text: ベルベルベルベルベルベット
translation: Vel-vel-vel-vel-vel-velvet…

text: 我が主長い花
translation: My lord, the long flower…
grammar: 我が is a classical/literary possessive pronoun, giving the lyric a formal, archaic flavor.

text: はいご一緒に
translation: Yes, let's sing together.
grammar: はい + ご一緒に is an invitation/prompt, with ご一緒に being the honorific form of 一緒に.

text: 本日は体験入学をさせていただき より一層世界観が広がりました
translation: Today, having been allowed to experience attending school, my view of the world has broadened all the more.
grammar: 〜させていただき is a humble construction ('having been graciously allowed to do'), used here to show deference to those who permitted the experience.

text: よろしければまたいつかご一緒させていただきたく存じます
translation: If it would be agreeable, I should very much like to accompany you again someday.

vocabulary.meaning: humble form of 思います (I think/feel)

grammar: 〜させていただきたく存じます is a very polite, layered expression of desire: causative + humble request (いただく) + たく (wish) + 存じます (humble 思う).

text: 実は私 なぜことさらにここを訪れたいと思ったのか
translation: The truth is, I myself am not entirely sure why I particularly wanted to visit here.
grammar: なぜ〜か embedded in the main clause functions as an indirect question ('why it was that…'), creating a reflective, searching tone.

text: 自分でもよくわからない ですがあなたに身を寄せて歩いている間
translation: I am not entirely sure even myself — but during the time I walked by your side,

vocabulary.meaning: to draw close to, to lean in to

grammar: ですが here is a conjunctive ('but / however'), pivoting from confession of uncertainty to the warm experience that followed.

text: 私 なんというか / とても充実しておりましたもしかすると私はあなたのことをよく知りたいのかもしれません
translation: I felt — how shall I put it — very fulfilled. It may be that I wish to know you better.
grammar: なんというか ('how shall I put it') is a hesitation filler that here conveys genuine emotional searching rather than mere habit, softening the confession that follows.

text: 一体どうしてっ ともあれこの原因を究明するまでは退屈せずに済みそうか
translation: But whatever could it be? In any case, until I get to the bottom of this cause, it seems I shall not be bored.

vocabulary.meaning: in any case, be that as it may
to investigate thoroughly, to get to the bottom of

grammar: 〜ずに済む means 'to get by without doing ~'; here 退屈せずに済みそう = 'it seems I can get by without being bored.'

text: では戻るといたしましょう お疲れ様でございました
translation: Well then, let us return. You have worked hard today — thank you.

vocabulary.meaning: thank you for your efforts; well done

grammar: 〜といたしましょう is a very polite volitional ('let us do ~'), using the humble いたす in place of する.

text: ふふっ
translation: Heheh…

text: お待ちしておりました
translation: I have been waiting for you.

vocabulary.word: お待ちしておりました
vocabulary.reading: おまちしておりました
vocabulary.meaning: I have been waiting (humble, polite past)

grammar: お待ちしておりました is a humble-polite form: お + 待ち + する (humble) + おる (humble continuous) + ました, expressing respectful anticipation.

text: ここがあなたの住んでいる学生寮ですね
translation: This is the student dormitory where you live, isn't it.
grammar: 〜ですね is a sentence-final particle seeking gentle confirmation, fitting Elizabeth's characteristically observational manner.

text: ここがあなたの部屋 / 見慣れないものに囲まれておりますね
translation: So this is your room — you are surrounded by things unfamiliar to me.
grammar: 見慣れない is formed from 見慣れる (to get used to seeing) negated; the progressive passive 囲まれておりますね adds polite observation of a present state.

text: ところであなたの部屋に出かけたいという私の依頼についてですが
translation: By the way, regarding my request to visit your room —
grammar: 〜についてですが uses について ('regarding') followed by ですが as a topic-raising conjunction, signalling that something important is about to be said.

text: そのご不審に思われませんでしたか
translation: Did that not strike you as suspicious?

vocabulary.meaning: to be thought, to seem (honorific passive)

grammar: ご不審に思われませんでしたか: ご + 不審 (honorific prefix), 思われる (honorific/passive of 思う), past negative question — 'did you not find it suspicious?'

text: そうでしたか / 実は私降り行ってお話ししたいことが
translation: Is that so? The truth is, I came here because there is something I wished to speak with you about.

vocabulary.meaning: specifically, purposefully, taking special care (to come/go)

grammar: 降り行って (折り入って) is a set phrase meaning 'with a specific and important purpose,' emphasizing the gravity of what she is about to share.

text: こちらの世界を探望して私は多くのものに触れました / 何もかもが忘れられない思い出
translation: Exploring this world, I have touched so many things — each and every one an irreplaceable memory,

vocabulary.meaning: to touch, to come into contact with

grammar: 何もかもが忘れられない思い出 is a nominal phrase ('memories that are unforgettable, every single one'), functioning as a predicate with the subject elided.

text: きらめく光珠のようでございます
translation: Like glittering, shining jewels of light.
grammar: 〜のようでございます is a very formal simile construction ('it is as though / like ~'), here continuing the preceding sentence poetically.

text: にぎわう街並みを歩いたり / 食を楽しんだり神社で無邪気に過ごして
translation: Walking through the bustling streets, savoring food, spending carefree time at the shrine,

vocabulary.meaning: townscape, row of buildings along a street

grammar: The 〜たり〜たり construction lists actions as representative examples ('doing such things as walking and eating'), building up to the emotional climax.

text: あなたの学校にも行って / そして私気がついたのでございます
translation: I also went to your school — and then I realized something.

vocabulary.meaning: to notice, to realize, to become aware

grammar: 〜のでございます is a formal explanatory/emphatic sentence ending, giving her realization a slightly solemn, declarative weight.

text: 私は無意識に依頼の回を追うごとに
translation: I had been, without realizing it, with each successive outing,

vocabulary.meaning: to follow, to go through in sequence

grammar: 回を追うごとに means 'with each successive time/round,' using ごとに ('each time') to indicate gradual progression.

text: よりあなたに近しい場所を指定しておりました / ですから本日はこちらの世界で最も深くあなたを知り得る場所
translation: Specifying places ever closer to you — and so today, the place in this world where I could come to know you most deeply:

vocabulary.meaning: to be able to know, to come to know

grammar: よりあなたに近しい場所を指定しておりました: the 〜ておりました (humble progressive past) captures the ongoing, unconscious pattern; ですから pivots to the emotional conclusion.

text: あなたの部屋に出かけたいと依頼させていただいた次第でございます
translation: That is how I came to humbly request permission to visit your room.
grammar: 〜させていただいた次第でございます: ultra-formal closing formula explaining the reason/circumstance for an action — 'that is the reason I ventured to do X.'

text: 失礼いたします
translation: Pardon the intrusion.

text: 覚えておいてでしょうか / 以前学校を案内していただいたり
translation: Do you remember — how you once showed me around your school?
grammar: 〜ていただく: humble form of 〜てもらう — 'to have someone kindly do something for one.'

text: あなたに触れた私が充実を感じると申し上げたこと
translation: — and how I told you that, upon touching your world, I felt a sense of fulfillment?

vocabulary.meaning: to touch, to come into contact with

grammar: 〜と申し上げたこと: nominalised quotation ('the fact that I said X') functioning as the object of 覚えておいて in idx 152.

text: 私にとってああいった心境の変化は初めてのことでございました
translation: That kind of change of heart was something I had never experienced before.
grammar: ああいった: 'that sort of, like that' — a demonstrative modifier referring back to what was just described.

text: どうして私は充実を感じたのか
translation: Why was it that I felt such fulfillment?
grammar: 〜のか: nominalizing question particle expressing rhetorical wonder or internal pondering.

text: 私こちらを訪れてようやくその疑問の答えにたどり着きました
translation: It was only by visiting here that I finally managed to arrive at the answer to that question.

vocabulary.meaning: to finally reach, to arrive at after effort

grammar: 〜てようやく: 'only after doing X did Y finally occur' — ようやく adds a sense of at last/barely.

text: 答えは実感だと存じます
translation: The answer, I believe, is lived experience — reality felt firsthand.

vocabulary.meaning: lived sensation, sense of reality, firsthand feeling

grammar: 〜と存じます: humble equivalent of 〜と思います — Elizabeth's characteristic polite assertion.

text: ベルベットルームの住人である者が心待ちにするのは客人
translation: For those who dwell in the Velvet Room, what we look forward to is our guests —

vocabulary.meaning: to look forward to, to eagerly await

grammar: Sentence breaks mid-thought (continued in idx 159–160); 〜である者が: relative clause 'those who are X.'

text: その訪れだけが外界との接点であり
translation: — their visits are our sole point of contact with the outside world,
grammar: 〜のみが: 'only X' — emphatic restriction. Sentence continues in idx 160.

text: 私どもに意義を与える / こうしてあなたに触れることで私はそれを得るのでございます
translation: — and what gives us meaning. By touching your life in this way, I gain just that.
grammar: こうして〜ことで: 'by doing X in this way' — instrumental conjunction linking the means to the result.

text: いっそありていに申し上げます
translation: Allow me to be perfectly candid.

vocabulary.meaning: rather; all the more; just to go ahead and

grammar: いっそありていに申し上げます: 'let me just go ahead and say it plainly' — いっそ intensifies the decision to be frank.

text: 私世間知らずゆえに色々ととんきょなこともあったかとは存じますが / さすがに私でも殿方の資質に上がり込む意味くらいは存じております
translation: I am sure there were moments when my inexperience with the world led to some rather outlandish behavior on my part — yet even I understand well enough the meaning of accepting an invitation into a gentleman's private quarters.

vocabulary.meaning: inexperienced in the ways of the world, naive
to enter someone's home uninvited; to step up into a private room

grammar: 〜ゆえに: classical/formal causal conjunction 'because of, owing to' — characteristic of Elizabeth's archaic register.

text: もしあなたさえよろしければお手引きをいただきたいのです
translation: If it would be acceptable to you, I would very much like you to show me the way.

vocabulary.meaning: if it pleases you, if you don't mind (polite conditional)

grammar: もしあなたさえよろしければ: 'if only it is agreeable to you' — さえ here adds 'so long as, as long as only.'

text: ありがとうございます / ございます
translation: Thank you. Thank you so much.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございます
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございます

text: 初めてこちらの世界に来た頃とは
translation: Compared to when I first came to this world —

vocabulary.meaning: around the time of, the period when

grammar: 〜とは: contrastive topic marker — sets up the comparison continued in idx 166.

text: まるで別人になった自分がいる気がいたします
translation: — I feel as though I have become a completely different person.

vocabulary.meaning: a different person, someone else entirely

grammar: まるで〜気がいたします: 'it feels just as if' — まるで reinforces the simile; いたします is humble いたす.

text: これ以上こちらに留まっては / 己の本来の役割を忘れてしまいそう
translation: If I were to linger here any longer, I feel I might forget my true role.

vocabulary.meaning: to remain, to stay, to linger

grammar: 〜ては〜そう: 'if I were to keep doing X, it seems Y would happen' — ては indicates an undesirable conditional.

text: ですがそれはあなたにとっても不利益
translation: And that would be to your detriment as well.
grammar: Elliptical predicate: あなたにとっても不利益 ('also a disadvantage for you') — subject and verb are omitted but understood from context.

text: ですからこちらの世界を巡り歩くのは
translation: And so, wandering through this world —

vocabulary.meaning: to wander through, to go around visiting

grammar: Sentence continues in idx 170; 〜のは: nominalizes the verb phrase as the topic ('as for wandering this world...').

text: これを最後にさせていただきたいと存じます
translation: — I would like to make this the last time.
grammar: 〜にさせていただきたいと存じます: layered humility — causative + いただく + たい + と存じます, expressing a polite wish/decision.

text: 私の好奇心に最後までお付き合いいただき
translation: Thank you for indulging my curiosity all the way to the end —

vocabulary.meaning: to the very end, all the way through
to humbly have someone accompany/indulge one

grammar: 〜に最後までお付き合いいただき: humble form of 'having you keep me company/indulge me to the end' — sentence continues in idx 172.

text: 本当にありがとうございました / 本当に
translation: — I truly, truly thank you.

vocabulary.word: ありがとうございました
vocabulary.reading: ありがとうございました

grammar: Past tense ありがとうございました marks the formal close of a completed experience — more final than the present-tense form.

text: それでは名残惜しいですが参りましょう
translation: Well then — it is hard to part, but let us be on our way.

vocabulary.meaning: reluctant to part, hating to say goodbye
let us go (humble volitional of 行く)

grammar: それでは: 'well then / in that case' — conventional transition to a farewell or departure. 参る is the humble equivalent of 行く.
